chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Murzam ibn Hakim who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The Mu'tammir (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') enters Mecca on the night of Arafah, and the menstruating woman; when does the 'Umrah of Tamattu' become due for them both? He said: 'When the people reach Mina.'

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: The 'Umrah of Tamattu' (the specific ritual act)
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ عَرَفَةَ: The night of Arafah (8th Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When does the Umrah of Tamattu' become effective for the pilgrim and the menstruating woman?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise moment the state of *Ihram* for *Umrat al-Tamattu'* is formally established, linking it to the gathering at Mina rather than mere entry into Mecca. This distinction is crucial for understanding the legal status of the pilgrim and the menstruating woman who may enter early, ensuring their *Umrah* is validly completed only after reaching the designated station. The hadith underscores the practical application of ritual timing in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the spiritual and legal obligations are tied to the specific location of Mina on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah.
